stories.title: JLL, Cousins Link Up on Two Austin Office Transactions
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets completed two Austin, Texas, transactions with Cousins Properties. JLL arranged the sale of Research Park Plaza V, a 172,854-square-foot office building in Austin’s Northwest submarket, and secured a preferred equity placement for 5th & Walsh, a 198,000-square-foot Class A office and retail development in the West 5th Street corridor. In the Research Park Plaza V sale, JLL Capital Markets’ Ryan Stevens, Drew Fuller and Jeff Coddington represented Cousins Properties to complete the sale to an unnamed buyer. Developed in 2015, Research Park Plaza V is a Class A, four-story office asset that is 85% leased to four institutional-quality tenants. For the 5th and Walsh development, JLL Capital Markets’ Stevens, Robert Wooten and Colby Mueck worked on behalf of Endeavor Real Estate Group (the developer) to arrange a $31.5 million preferred equity commitment through Cousins Properties. It will be Endeavor’s HQ. 5th & Walsh is a five-story, ground-up development totaling 198,000 rentable square feet, comprising approximately 177,000 square feet of Class A office and approximately 21,000 square feet of ground-floor retail. The post JLL, Cousins Link Up on Two Austin Office Transactions appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranged sale of Research Park Plaza V, 172,854-sf Austin office, 85% leased.
JLL secured $31.5M preferred equity for 5th & Walsh, 198,000-sf mixed-use development.
Endeavor Real Estate Group relocating HQ to Austin West 5th Street corridor.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets completed two Austin office transactions for Cousins Properties: the sale of Research Park Plaza V, a 172,854-square-foot Class A office building that is 85% leased to institutional tenants, and a $31.5 million preferred equity placement for 5th & Walsh, a 198,000-square-foot mixed-use development that will serve as Endeavor Real Estate Group's headquarters. The 5th & Walsh project comprises 177,000 square feet of Class A office and 21,000 square feet of ground-floor retail across five stories.
stories.impact: HQ relocation of a major developer to Austin West 5th Street signals continued corporate in-migration and talent concentration in that submarket, strengthening long-term multifamily demand. The willingness of capital (Cousins) to deploy $31.5M in preferred equity for office-retail development suggests mixed-use anchoring is viewed as resilient in Austin's best submarkets, but multifamily operators should monitor if office space remains underutilized post-relocation—any major lease rollover or sublease activity could signal softening demand in that corridor.

stories.title: U.S. Industrial Demand Could Exceed Supply by Late 2027
stories.excerpt: The U.S. industrial market could reach a turning point in late 2027, CoStar reported. Vacancy is expected to rise slightly through the early part of next year before making a gradual descent, with demand beginning to outpace supply late in the year. The national industrial vacancy rate remains in the mid-7% range entering the third quarter of 2026 and is expected to edge higher before beginning a steady decline. CoStar characterized this outlook as a modest improvement from the previous forecast, as stronger-than-expected demand in recent quarters has led to an upward revision in near-term net absorption and a slightly lower vacancy outlook. “While leasing activity remains healthy, elevated availability and a lingering supply overhang are expected to keep rent growth modest in the near term,” said Juan Arias, national director of industrial analytics at CoStar Group. “By late 2027, slowing construction activity and improving demand should allow net absorption to exceed new supply, marking a turning point for market fundamentals.” Average annual rent growth over the 2026-27 period has also been revised higher and is now forecasted at +1.9%. The post U.S. Industrial Demand Could Exceed Supply by Late 2027 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. industrial vacancy mid-7% entering Q3 2026, expected to rise early 2027.
CoStar forecasts demand to outpace supply by late 2027, marking turnaround.
Annual rent growth 2026–27 revised upward to +1.9%, modest but improving.
stories.summary: CoStar Group reports the U.S. industrial market will reach a turning point in late 2027 when demand begins to exceed supply. National industrial vacancy is expected to edge higher through early 2027 before declining steadily, driven by stronger-than-expected demand in recent quarters and a slowdown in construction activity. Average annual rent growth over 2026–27 has been revised upward to +1.9%, reflecting modest but improving fundamentals.
stories.impact: This forecast has limited direct bearing on multifamily development but signals the broader CRE financing and construction environment: if industrial supply softens and cap rates tighten post-2027, capital will reallocate away from industrial toward other asset classes, potentially increasing multifamily equity availability and lowering cost of capital for multifamily developers in 2027–28. Monitor industrial starts and lender appetite now—a shift suggests capital recycling is imminent.

stories.title: Concord Arranges $50M Construction Loan for FW Apartments
stories.excerpt: Summa Terra Ventures and M13 Construction obtained a $50 million construction loan for Vic Centre Apartments, a 268-unit Class A multifamily community in Fort Worth. Concord Summit Managing Director David Larson and Director Keegan Burger arranged the financing on behalf of the project sponsor. The financing was structured as an 80% loan-to-cost capital stack, combining senior construction debt with mezzanine financing. Vic Centre Apartments will rise at 7124 Anderson Blvd. in East Fort Worth, 15 minutes from downtown Fort Worth. The community will span nine three-story buildings, offering a mix of studios, one-bedroom and two-bedroom units, along with premium amenities. Construction has already begun and is expected to be completed within 24 months.   The post Concord Arranges $50M Construction Loan for FW Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Summa Terra Ventures and M13 Construction closed $50M construction loan for 268-unit Fort Worth project.
Vic Centre Apartments, 80% LTC structure, spans 9 three-story buildings, construction underway.
East Fort Worth location, 15 minutes from downtown; delivery expected within 24 months.
stories.summary: Concord Summit arranged a $50 million construction loan for Vic Centre Apartments, a 268-unit Class A multifamily community in East Fort Worth developed by Summa Terra Ventures and M13 Construction. The financing was structured as an 80% loan-to-cost capital stack combining senior debt and mezzanine financing. Construction is underway on the nine three-story buildings with mixed-bedroom units and premium amenities, with completion expected in 24 months.
stories.impact: Active construction financing in East Fort Worth submarket confirms lender confidence in outbound secondary markets and mid-supply development. The 80% LTC and dual-layer capital stack are typical of current underwriting; watch if construction advances on schedule—any delay signals cost inflation or labor constraints in the DFW market. This project's delivery window (late 2027–early 2028) positions it to capture absorption ahead of CoStar's industrial supply tightening, when employment migration to Fort Worth may accelerate.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Sets Second-Quarter Revenue Record
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield said Wednesday that its second-quarter earnings were strong enough to boost the commercial real estate services giant’s per-share earnings guidance for the year. “Our results this year demonstrated that we have hit our stride, and we’ve gotten there fast,” C&W CEO Michelle MacKay said Wednesday during the company’s earnings call. “We didn’t just meet the bar this quarter; we moved it, setting several company records, including the highest second-quarter total revenue in the history of the company, the highest second-quarter leasing and services revenue in the history of the company, and the lowest gross debt balance in the history of the company.” Revenue for the second quarter of 2026 grew by 11 percent year over year to $2.8 billion, while adjusted diluted earnings per share (EPS) grew 17 percent annually to 35 cents per share. C&W’s revenue for the second quarter of 2026 topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.6 percent, while EPS just missed the 36 cents per share analysts were expecting. “We achieved our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Back in December, at our investor day, we laid out our current three-year growth plan and provided annual EPS targets. Today, just two quarters later, we are raising our guidance for year one,” MacKay said during the call. “And here’s what excites us most: This performance is organic, driven by a global platform with significant white space still ahead.” Annual adjusted earnings per share guidance has been adjusted to reflect expected growth of between 18 percent and 23 percent, compared with C&W’s previous guidance of between 15 percent and 20 percent growth for the year. Leasing activity was strong this quarter, with leasing revenue growing by 27 percent year-over-year to $628.5 million. bullets: Cushman & Wakefield Q2 2026 revenue $2.8B, up 11% YoY; EPS 35¢, up 17%.
Company set records: highest Q2 revenue, highest Q2 leasing revenue, lowest gross debt ever.
Results topped Zacks consensus estimate by 4.6%; guidance raised for full year.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $2.8 billion, up 11% year-over-year, and adjusted diluted EPS of 35 cents, up 17% annually. The company achieved multiple records including highest Q2 revenue and leasing revenue in its history, and lowest gross debt balance on record. Results exceeded analyst consensus and prompted management to raise full-year earnings guidance.
stories.impact: Strong broker performance and capital velocity at C&W—a major originator of multifamily debt and equity placement—signals robust financing availability and fee-generation appetite in the CRE market. Rising Q2 leasing revenue suggests healthy deal flow across all sectors; for multifamily developers, this translates to competitive debt terms and active equity sourcing. Monitor if C&W's improved balance sheet (lowest debt ever) leads to expansion of in-house capital or warehouse facilities, which could reduce costs for developers sourcing construction or bridge financing.

stories.title: Zenith IOS, JPMAM Seal $215M Credit Facility With KeyBank, Truist
stories.excerpt: Zenith IOS, JPMAM Seal $215M Credit Facility With KeyBank, Truist As the industrial outdoor storage space continues to gain momentum, some key players are celebrating the next phase of their partnership with a fresh round of financing. Zenith Industrial Outdoor Storage and J.P. Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) just secured a $215 million credit facility from KeyBank and Truist, Commercial Observer can first report. The facility finances Zenith’s second programmatic joint venture with JPMAM and will allow the continued scaling of its expanding IOS portfolio. KeyBank served as administrative agent on the senior secured facility — which includes an accordion feature, allowing the JV to increase its borrowing capacity as needed — and led the transaction, while Truist served as joint lead arranger. Cooper-Horowitz’s Justin Horowitz, Ben Knopf and Josh Tropper arranged the facility. “This credit facility marks another significant milestone in our ongoing partnership with J.P. Morgan Asset Management, and reflects the continued institutional belief in the IOS sector,” Ben Atkins, co-founder and CEO of Zenith, said in a statement. “The scale and flexibility of this financing will allow us to accelerate acquisitions, deepen our presence in key growth markets, and continue executing on our long-term investment strategy. We are excited to build upon the success of our first joint venture and further strengthen this second programmatic partnership.” The facility refinances 34 IOS assets spanning 140 acres. The majority of the properties are spread across Southeast, South Central and Southwest markets, and the portfolio is almost fully leased at 99.6 percent. It’s not the first time the JV has teamed up with KeyBank. In February, the lender also provided a $130 million credit facility to Zenith and JPMAM for a portfolio of 14 IOS properties. stories.summary: Zenith Industrial Outdoor Storage and J.P. Morgan Asset Management closed a $215 million senior secured credit facility with KeyBank (administrative agent and lead arranger) and Truist (joint lead arranger). The capital supports expansion of Zenith's industrial outdoor storage platform.
stories.impact: IOS is a micro-segment adjacent to multifamily but gaining institutional capital (JPMAM anchor + bank co-leads). The accordion structure and repeat JV signal lender and sponsor confidence in the asset class, which may crowd out marginal multifamily players competing for similar credit terms and capital stack creativity. For multifamily developers in secondary markets with land costs rising, IOS competition for acreage and construction capital is a growing headwind; monitor local IOS development pipelines in your target markets.

stories.title: Brook Farm Inks $73M Refi on Covington Apartments
stories.excerpt: Brook Farm Group refinanced The Sinclair at Callaway Farm, a 388-unit, Class A multifamily community in Covington, Georgia. The $73 million refinancing from Prime Finance replaces the initial construction loan and preferred equity investment from the project’s inception in 2023. The refinancing was facilitated by Shawn Rosenthal, Jason Gaccione, and Jake Salkovitz of CBRE’s Debt & Structured Finance group. The Sinclair includes one-, two-, and three-bedroom units with luxury finishes, a 9,000-square-foot clubhouse, a pool, an expansive two-story gym, co-working space, a dog park, a pet spa, fast-charging EV stations, and the first rooftop lounge in the market. The Sinclair at Callaway Farm was Brook Farm Group’s first development following the launch of the company in 2022. The community was completed in Q2 2025. Since the company’s launch, Brook Farm Group has added five multifamily developments in various stages of construction and lease-up across Georgia and Florida, totaling over 1,500 units. The post Brook Farm Inks $73M Refi on Covington Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brook Farm Group refinanced The Sinclair at Callaway Farm, 388-unit Covington, GA, for $73M.

stories.summary: Brook Farm Group refinanced The Sinclair at Callaway Farm, a 388-unit Class A multifamily community in Covington, Georgia, for $73 million through Prime Finance. The refinancing replaces the initial construction loan and preferred equity from the project's inception in 2023. The community was completed in Q2 2025 and features luxury one-, two-, and three-bedroom units with extensive amenities including a rooftop lounge.
stories.impact: Successful stabilization refi 12+ months post-completion signals strong lease-up, rent achievement, and operator track record in suburban Atlanta. Brook Farm's portfolio growth to 1,500+ units in Georgia and Florida over 3 years demonstrates capital market confidence in secondary markets; the $73M refi at 388 units (~$188k per unit) indicates solid value creation. Watch Brook Farm's next funding round—rapid pipeline growth often precedes scale-up of construction financing, signaling availability of capital for similar-profile developers in Atlanta and Florida growth corridors.

stories.title: RIVANI Adds to Miami Beach Holdings
stories.excerpt: RIVANI purchased 404 Washington, an 8-story mixed-use office and retail property positioned at the gateway to Miami Beach’s South of Fifth neighborhood. The Trump Group was the seller. Comprising nearly 61,000 square feet of office and retail space, 404 Washington occupies the corner of Washington Avenue and Fifth Street. Built in 1995 and renovated in 2026, the property’s tenant roster includes Universal Music Group, Marriott Vacations Worldwide, 26North, and Major Food Group’s HaSalon restaurant. Berkadia Miami’s Brad Williamson, Scott Wadler and Michael Basinski, along with Mitch Sinberg, Matt Robbins, and Jacob Kelly, secured $29.5 million in financing on behalf of RIVANI. BridgeInvest provided the loan. Berkadia’s Basinski added, “Opportunities to acquire an asset of this caliber in the South of Fifth neighborhood are extraordinarily rare, which made this an attractive opportunity for both the sponsor and the lending community.” The post RIVANI Adds to Miami Beach Holdings appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RIVANI purchased 404 Washington, 61,000-sf mixed-use office/retail in Miami Beach South of Fifth.
Property 1995-built, renovated 2026; tenants include Universal Music Group, Marriott Vacations, Major Food Group.

stories.summary: RIVANI acquired 404 Washington, an 8-story mixed-use property comprising nearly 61,000 square feet of office and retail space at the gateway to Miami Beach's South of Fifth neighborhood. The building, built in 1995 and renovated in 2026, houses institutional tenants including Universal Music Group, Marriott Vacations Worldwide, and Major Food Group's HaSalon restaurant. Berkadia secured $29.5 million in financing from BridgeInvest on behalf of the buyer.
stories.impact: Institutional-grade office/retail asset changing hands at corner of Fifth & Washington signals South of Fifth's continued absorption of commercial capital and mixed-use development. This submarket's concentration of entertainment, hospitality, and corporate tenants creates upward pressure on nearby residential values and day-time population density—a tailwind for multifamily operators in Miami Beach and Wynwood who benefit from amenity clustering and urban foot traffic. Multifamily developers should note Miami Beach's increasingly mixed-use, experiential character as justification for premium rents and ground-floor retail integration in new residential projects.

stories.summary: A podcast featuring Stake CEO Rowland Hobbs explores how renter loyalty and cash-back programs drive multifamily net operating income. Topics include why rent was historically excluded from loyalty programs, the rise of financial amenities versus flashy perks, cash-back incentives for retention and delinquency prevention, and vertical integration opportunities in multifamily. The discussion also covers competitors like Bilt Rewards and the impact of rising housing costs on renter churn.
stories.impact: Not material to development underwriting or capital deployment, but signals an emerging operational lever: fintech-driven resident retention and yield management may influence underwriting assumptions on turnover costs, lease renewal rates, and NOI sensitivity. Developers should incorporate resident engagement tech (loyalty, cash-back, or similar) into operating model pro formas, especially in high-churn, cost-sensitive submarkets. Stake's focus on UMoveFree acquisition in Texas also signals consolidation in multifamily service tech—monitor if operational tech become commoditized, reducing competitive moats for operators.

stories.title: Volastra Therapeutics Subleases 18K SF at Alexandria Center for Life Science
stories.excerpt: A biotechnology firm is relocating its lab space from West Harlem to Midtown South. Volastra Therapeutics signed an 18,120-square-foot lease in the Alexandria Center for Life Science at 430 East 29th Street, owned by Alexandria Real Estate Equities, according to CBRE. Volastra is subleasing space on the 11th floor from Black Diamond Therapeutics and relocating from the Mink Building at 1361-1369 Amsterdam Avenue in Harlem. CBRE did not disclose the asking rent for the sublease, but the average office asking rent in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a CBRE report. “Volastra’s decision to establish its operations at the Alexandria Center for Life Science is a testament to the company’s momentum and long-term vision,” CBRE’s Joe DeRosa, who negotiated on behalf of the subtenant, said in a statement. “This transaction provides Volastra with best-in-class laboratory infrastructure in a premier location and supports the company’s next stage of scientific and corporate growth.” CBRE’s John Isaacs negotiated on behalf of Black Diamond. Volastra isn’t the only one in the dynamic seeing growth. Alexandria reported earnings on Tuesday in which executives expressed optimism after several depressed quarters, mainly attributed to oversaturation in the life sciences market following the pandemic and funding cuts to scientific research at the federal level. Alexandria is seeing an uptick in leasing momentum across its portfolio. Much like with this sublease, a significant portion of that has been in backfilling recently vacated space. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Volastra Therapeutics subleased 18,120 sf at Alexandria Center for Life Science, Midtown South.
Relocation from West Harlem (Mink Building) to 11th floor, 430 East 29th Street.
Q2 2026 Midtown South office asking rent averaged $85.73/sf; Alexandria REIT reporting strong earnings.
stories.summary: Biotechnology firm Volastra Therapeutics signed an 18,120-square-foot sublease at the Alexandria Center for Life Science at 430 East 29th Street in Midtown South, relocating from the Mink Building in West Harlem. Volastra is subleasing from Black Diamond Therapeutics on the 11th floor. While the specific sublease rent was not disclosed, Midtown South office asking rent averaged $85.73 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Life sciences tenancy migration from West Harlem (secondary) to Midtown South (primary life science cluster) at Alexandria REIT's flagship property underscores the concentration of biotech talent and amenities in NYC's premier lab markets. For multifamily developers near East 29th Street and the Alexandria campus, this signals sustained job growth and young professional in-migration; similarly positioned residential projects should emphasize proximity to life sciences employment. However, the rise in Midtown South office asking rent ($85.73/sf) also reflects capital competition and pricing power in knowledge-worker clusters—multifamily rents in adjacent neighborhoods (Kips Bay, Gramercy) will track upward in tandem with office fundamentals and talent influx.

stories.title: Mall Giant Macerich Narrows Losses in Q2 Amid Stronger Leasing
stories.excerpt: “No one is building new regional malls, and roughly 90 percent of our go-forward NOI comes from Class A assets and the best retailers of the world.” So said Jackson Hsieh, president and CEO of Macerich, early on during the mall-focused real estate investment trust’s second-quarter earnings call Tuesday afternoon. (He was referring to projected net operating income.) The observation goes a long way toward explaining the REIT’s continued turnaround. Macerich owns 40 million square feet of real estate, most of it within 37 malls in markets in California, the Pacific Northwest, and the Washington-to-New York corridor. Hsieh took over the company in early 2024 when it was struggling to maintain tenancies at some of the malls, a few of which Macerich has since sold. Meanwhile, development of fresh shopping centers in these prime markets has all but dried up, leaving Macerich and only a handful of competitors such as Simon Property Group at the top of a tighter market amid ongoing demand from Gen Zers and other shoppers. Macerich reported leased occupancy of 94 percent in the second quarter, up from 92 percent during the same period in 2025. The REIT signed around 1.3 million square feet of new and renewal leases. That led to what Macerich described as 1 percent annual increase in the second quarter of new-store square footage. The REIT expects approximately $124 million in total gross revenue from these new-store leases. Leasing deals included with tenants such as Aerie, Offline by Aerie, Old Navy, Eataly, Zara and Sephora. It also included tenants in the increasingly popular experiential retail niche such as Level 99 and Golf Galaxy. The REIT’s revenue from leases was $233.4 million in the second quarter, up slightly from $232.7 in the second quarter of 2025. Total revenue was $249.7 million, about the same as last year. bullets: Macerich narrowed Q2 losses amid stronger leasing; 94% leased occupancy achieved.
CEO Jackson Hsieh cites competitive moat: no new regional malls; 90% NOI from Class A.

stories.summary: Macerich reported improved Q2 results with leased occupancy of 94% as the mall REIT benefits from a structural advantage: virtually no new regional malls are being built in its markets. CEO Jackson Hsieh noted that roughly 90% of forward NOI comes from Class A assets and top-tier retailers. The REIT owns 40 million square feet across 37 malls in California, the Pacific Northwest, and the Washington-to-New York corridor.
stories.impact: Not directly material to multifamily development, but signals that traditional enclosed malls are consolidating around premium, anchored properties in dense urban and first-ring suburban corridors—precisely the markets where multifamily developers operate. Macerich's dominance and pricing power in gateway markets (CA, Northeast corridor) may compress retail availability and increase rents for ground-floor multifamily retail tenants. Additionally, the absence of new competitive retail construction in these prime markets suggests limited development headroom overall and tighter capital allocation, which could accelerate multifamily's relative appeal to investors and lenders seeking yield in the same markets.
